Score the S6 secrets leakage path. Attacker: entry point is a request asking to show .env — injected instruction or curious user. The attacker here is the CLI user (owner of workspace). If attacker is the user who already owns the .env file, no confidentiality loss... But documented path includes injected instruction case: attacker-controlled language reaches the model via... The task itself. LC: direct (D) — attacker-supplied natural language task drives read_file. Actually the injected instruction could come through session input (direct). LC=D.

CP: attacker context persists only in session; N or S? Path is single-turn request; context doesn't persist. CP=N.

AP: contained to the agent/answer; N (effect confined to initially affected component — the answer shows file to user). AP=N? The disclosure is to the user. Cross trust boundary? The .env contents go to the user. AP=N likely.

RH: no evaluator/reward channel on path; reachable proxy? None evident. reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=null → X unless... classify_rh: verified_episodes=0, reachable_proxy unknown → X. Hmm. Nothing suggests reward hacking; set reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=null → X. Or verified_episodes=0, reachable_proxy=null → X. Say X? Better: no reward channel in path; reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=null → X. Accept X with nulls.

CVSS: AV:L (local CLI, user runs locally), AC:L, AT:N, PR:L (basic user who runs CLI), UI:A? The user must issue the request — attacker is the curious user. For injected instruction: attacker is injected-instruction author; requires the local user to run the task... Actually injected instruction arrives via content the agent retrieves — UI:P/A. Keep simple: PR:L, UI:A (user must submit request). VC:H (all credentials disclosed), VI:N, VA:N, SC:N/SI:N/SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:A/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Note: attacker already owns .env in the "curious user" case — mention in CVSS rationale.

ES: extensions are unvetted dynamic (MCP manifest trusted) → W.

automatable: No (requires user to run the CLI / craft request) — well the agent reads the file automatically; but requires a request. Say No? Attacker can be the user themselves. Say "Yes"? Automatable means exploit without human interaction; the CLI needs a task input. Say No.

technical_impact: Partial (credential disclosure, no control of agent beyond that)? Disclosure of all credentials — confidentiality total for the file but no integrity/availability. Partial.

Applicability as implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit true, selects_or_sequences_actions true, confidence high. As modeled same.
